summary.headline: Stylam's third laminate plant at Manak Tabra is due to start commercial production by end-June or early July 2026, with INR250-300 crore revenue targeted in FY27.
summary.overview: Management said the third greenfield laminate plant at Manak Tabra is in testing and should begin commercial production in late June or early July 2026, delayed from earlier guidance by an environment clearance issue. Total capex to date is INR334 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 20-25% over FY26 and said Q4 gross margin was about 49% (which an analyst later cited as 39%, a discrepancy unresolved on the call). The call was dominated by the AICA Japan open offer and strategic partnership, the impact of the West Asia war on raw material costs, and management's answers were often vague or hard to hear.

segments.name: Laminates (existing plants)
segments.commentary: Laminate capacity utilisation was 74% in FY26; management said existing orders are being delayed due to capacity constraints. Export is about 75% of revenue.

segments.name: New third laminate plant (Manak Tabra)
segments.commentary: Management guided INR250-300 crore revenue in FY27 and INR600-700 crore in FY28 at about 80% utilisation; peak utilisation could yield INR900-1,000 crore. Operating margin guided at 22-24%.

segments.name: Acrylics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue was about INR15 crore; FY27 target is INR50-70 crore, supported by AICA Japan purchasing acrylic, which management said is at a preliminary stage.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Management took over domestic handling about three months ago and does not report domestic EBITDA separately; the company reports consolidated EBITDA only.

guidance_outlook: Commercial production at new Manak Tabra plant expected end-June to early-July 2026; testing has started.
New plant revenue INR250-300 crore in FY27 (earlier stated INR300-400 crore in the next three quarters), INR600-700 crore in FY28 at about 80% utilisation.
Overall FY27 revenue growth guided at roughly 20-25% over FY26; management declined to give an exact number.
EBITDA margin for new plant expected at 22-24%; an analyst's suggestion of about 22% company-level EBITDA by FY28 was answered with 'hopefully'.
Management expects EBITDA impact from West Asia-driven cost increases to be limited to about 1-3%, offset by price hikes, higher revenue absorbing fixed costs, and favourable USD/EUR exchange rates.
AICA deal (open offer completion and remaining stake tender of about 40%) expected to finish by mid-June, after which collaboration will be discussed.
capex_capacity: Third greenfield laminate plant at Manak Tabra: construction largely complete; delayed from November, then March, now June due to environment clearance (EC) needed from the Ministry of Environment in Delhi because Haryana had no CER at the time.
Capex incurred to date INR334 crore; management said fixed costs for the new plant are already in the P&L and staffing is about 150 workers with ~70-80% of wage costs already set.
New plant: three of four lines dedicated to export; compact laminates; some sizes to be produced in India for the first time.
Ramp-up: 30-40% utilisation expected from Q2 FY27; 80%+ utilisation targeted within two years.
Management said next quarter it would outline further expansion plans; a planned expansion was mentioned but not detailed.
demand_pricing: Management said new customers for the new plant's sizes are in discussion but gave no quantified PO book; existing orders are being delayed due to capacity constraint.

Raw materials: phenol and paper costs rose due to Middle East supply disruption; management said melamine has 5-6 months stock, phenol was bought 3-4 months ago at old prices, and some chemicals are under forward contracts.
Price hikes: 3-5% taken across customers; domestic in two tranches; export only where feasible, as management said Stylam competes with European players less affected by commodity costs.
Management said demand is not expected to fall with price increases, citing construction demand.
Export shipments are on FOB terms; transit time 45-60 days; no shipping delays reported. US tariff 10%.
Domestic brand visibility: management expects results in two to three quarters after restructuring of domestic sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the new plant delayed and what is the commercial production date?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay was due to an environment clearance issue after a Supreme Court observation; EC was applied to the Ministry of Environment in Delhi, taking 2-3 months plus. Commercial production expected late June to early July; testing started.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue guidance for FY27 and what is the peak potential of the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: New plant FY27 revenue INR250-300 crore; FY28 INR600-700 crore at 80% utilisation; peak INR900-1,000 crore. Company-level FY27 growth 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will management structure or the AICA stake change after the open offer?
qa_highlights.answer: Manit Gupta said no change in management; AICA is a strategic partner with no operational role. Management said the aim is not to sell stake, though the SHA put option exists.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the West Asia war on costs and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said impact limited to 1-3% of EBITDA, offset by price hikes, revenue scale, and favourable exchange rates (USD near INR96, EUR near INR112). Q4 gross margin cited as 49%, later referenced as 39% by an analyst.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and FY26 export vs domestic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex to date INR334 crore. FY26 revenue split 75% export and 25% domestic; management expects to keep the same split in FY27 while growing domestic.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AICA Japan opportunity for supply and acrylics?
qa_highlights.answer: AICA Global is not currently buying from India and has its own plant in Rudrapur; deal not yet finished, expected in about a month. Acrylics FY27 target INR50-70 crore.

risks_watch: Commissioning slippage: plant has already been delayed from November, then March, now June; watch for commercial production start by end-June/early July.

Raw material and freight volatility from West Asia conflict (phenol, crude-linked inputs, ocean freight); management said forward contracts and price increases will cover impact but this is unquantified.
Ramp-up risk: 30-40% utilisation from Q2 FY27 and new customer onboarding for new sizes not quantified.
Management clarity: guidance figures varied across the call (FY27 new-plant revenue of INR300-400 crore vs INR250-300 crore), and management was hard to hear at multiple points.
AICA open offer completion and ~40% stake tender by mid-June, plus SHA put option; collaboration terms and any ownership change remain open.
US tariff review on July 1 and transit times of 45-60 days.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, April sales and the new plant, but cautious and sometimes evasive on exact numbers and on the AICA transaction. Management repeatedly gave ranges or deferred detail ('next quarter we will let you know'), and call audio quality was poor for several speakers.
key_quotes: So we are quite hopeful that we can get INR300 crores, INR400 crores turnover from this plant in the next 3 quarters.
We have at this moment done the capex of INR334 crores.
The tariff right now, US is 10%.
Next quarter, we will let you know what we are actually planning further ahead.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue up roughly 20-25% (midpoint ~22.5%), backed by the Manak Tabra plant (capex INR334 crore, commercial production end-June to mid-July, INR250-300 crore FY27 revenue) and acrylics (INR50-70 crore), but no quantified PO book was given and the plant timeline has slipped repeatedly.
